newsitem.title: USA: U.S. lawmaker queries Greenspan on check clearing.
newsitem.headline: U.S. lawmaker queries Greenspan on check clearing.

text.p: A member of the U.S. House of Representatives' banking committee has requested that Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan prove the Fed has not subsidize check clearing for the past three years.

"I would appreciate your cooperation in sending me the 1995, 1996 and 1997 monthly reports from the ITS (Interdistrict Transportation System) on cost/revenue matching prepared at the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston," Carolyn Maloney, Dem.-N.Y., said in a letter she sent to Greenspan on Monday. The Monetary Control Act of 1980 requires the Fed to recover all costs tied to the financial services it provides the banking sector and the public, such as check clearing services.

Maloney, who queried Greenspan on the issue when he testified before Congress last month, has sponsored a bill to prevent the Fed from subsidizing the specific stand-alone cost of transporting the estimated 25 billion checks the central bank clears every year.
Greenspan said during his Humphrey-Hawkins testimony that "for check services, as a group... (the Fed has) significant profits."
